title: A Nearly-Linear Time Algorithm for Minimizing Risk of Conflict in Social Networks

problem.claim: Minimize the risk of conflict in social networks by modifying the initial opinions of a small number of nodes.

gap.claim: The cubic-time greedy solution creates a computation challenge for large networks.

contributions.claim: Show that the combinatorial optimization objective is monotone and supermodular.
Propose a naive greedy algorithm with a (1-1/e) approximation ratio and cubic running time.
Develop a nearly linear-time algorithm with a (1-1/e-ε) approximation ratio for any ε>0 by integrating approximation strategies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on various real-world datasets demonstrate the reported efficiency and effectiveness of the algorithms.
The fast algorithm scales to networks with more than two million nodes and achieves up to 20x speed-up over the state-of-the-art algorithm.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online social-media interactions have increased, enabling opinion exchange and contributing to resistance and controversy around contentious issues.
The paper studies minimizing social-network conflict risk by changing the initial opinions of a small number of nodes.
The authors establish monotonicity and supermodularity, then give a cubic-time greedy algorithm with a (1-1/e) approximation ratio.
They add approximation strategies to obtain a nearly linear-time algorithm with a (1-1/e-ε) approximation ratio.
Reported experiments indicate effectiveness, large-network scalability, and up to 20x speed-up over the state-of-the-art algorithm.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the real-world datasets used.

The abstract does not describe the approximation strategies or the meaning of the error parameter beyond ε>0.
